overview: Pakistan is a country in South Asia. Its capital is Islamabad and its largest city is Karachi. Pakistan was created in 1947, when British India was divided, as a homeland for the region's Muslims. It is one of the most populous countries in the world. Urdu and English are its official languages, and cricket is the most popular sport.

geography.text: Northern Pakistan has some of the highest mountains on Earth, where the Himalayas, the Karakoram and the Hindu Kush meet; K2, the world's second-highest peak, is on its border with China. The Indus river flows south through the fertile plains of Punjab and Sindh to the Arabian Sea. The west has dry plateaus and mountains, and the south-east includes part of the Thar Desert.

history.text: The Indus Valley civilisation flourished in what is now Pakistan more than 4,000 years ago, at cities such as Mohenjo-daro. The region later formed part of the Mughal Empire and British India. Pakistan was created in 1947 under Muhammad Ali Jinnah, and East Pakistan broke away as Bangladesh in 1971. Pakistan has fought several wars with India, mainly over Kashmir, and both countries have nuclear weapons.

events.title: Pakistan created
events.text: Pakistan becomes independent at the partition of British India.

events.title: Bangladesh breaks away
events.text: East Pakistan becomes Bangladesh after a war.

events.title: Nuclear tests
events.text: Pakistan tests nuclear weapons weeks after India.

events.title: Malala's Nobel
events.text: Malala Yousafzai becomes the youngest Nobel Peace Prize winner.

government.text: Pakistan is a federal parliamentary republic. The National Assembly chooses the Prime Minister, and the President is head of state. The army has ruled directly for long periods and remains very powerful. No elected Prime Minister has completed a full five-year term.

economy.text: Pakistan's economy depends on farming, especially cotton, wheat and rice, and on textiles, which make up most of its exports. Money sent home by Pakistanis abroad is very important. It has needed repeated loans from the International Monetary Fund.

culture.text: Pakistan's culture includes Punjabi, Sindhi, Pashtun, Baloch and other peoples. Urdu is the national language, and English is also official. Qawwali, Sufi devotional music made famous by Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan, is loved worldwide. Pakistan has five of the world's 14 mountains above 8,000 metres, including K2.

items.title: K2
items.text: The world's second-highest mountain, at 8,611 metres.

items.title: Badshahi Mosque
items.text: A grand Mughal mosque in Lahore.

sport.text: Cricket is Pakistan's passion. It won the Cricket World Cup in 1992 under Imran Khan, who later became Prime Minister, and the T20 World Cup in 2009. Field hockey brought three Olympic golds, and javelin thrower Arshad Nadeem won gold with an Olympic record in 2024.
